resolution_raising:
(A) R2-r1-1: in trees decided >=2.0, snake_case annotations are now read as declarations (⊥/malformed → explicit upper bound). Grounds: in mcp 2.2.0, ToolAnnotations has alias_generator=to_camel and validate_by_name, and I confirmed that read_only_hint=True goes out on the wire as {"readOnlyHint": true} (the dict form does too). How the version is decided (entries.mcp_version_class): API-shape evidence for >=2 is an import of mcp.server.mcpserver / mcp.server.MCPServer (these do not exist in 1.30.0), a Server(on_call_tool=) whose Server resolves to mcp, or the SDK 3-argument add_request_handler. Evidence for <2 is an import of mcp.server.fastmcp / mcp.server.FastMCP (ModuleNotFoundError in 2.x) or @x.call_tool(). Pin evidence comes from enforcement.mcp_major_votes, which votes per file across all dependency files: lock files, == / ~= / >=2 / <2, and fastmcp>=4 (fastmcp-slim 4.0.10 METADATA says mcp>=2). If any single piece of evidence points the other way, the result is unknown. So shims, shape/lock conflicts, monorepos whose lock files disagree, and stale locks all become unknown. When both spellings appear, camelCase wins (confirmed on 2.2.0). The pin parser handles PEP 508 extras and rejects prefixed names such as fastapi-mcp. Points an adversarial reviewer could attack: `mcp>=2` is not an exact pin but I treat it as deciding "major version >= 2"; imports inside test/example files also count as evidence (only toward unknown); a ToolAnnotations/dict passed to something other than an mcp framework is still converted.
(B) R2-r3-1: the handler's second positional parameter (self/cls excluded) is seeded as Obj(mcp.types.CallToolRequestParams; name=MODEL Atom, arguments=MODEL Map) at MODEL/resolved, so params.arguments[...] goes from MODEL/opaque to MODEL/resolved. Grounds: SDK 2.x calls the handler positionally as handler(ctx, CallToolRequestParams.model_validate(...)), and low-level 2.x does not enforce inputSchema. Seeding happens only when all four conditions hold: (i) every registration of that handler is SDK-shaped (Server resolves via the import table to mcp.server[.lowlevel[.server]].Server and that module is not in the tree, or add_request_handler's params_type resolves to mcp / mcp_types .CallToolRequestParams); (ii) the definition has no decorators (counterexample A3); (iii) it has at least 2 positional parameters; (iv) if it was found by bare-name matching, it matches the handler expression's form (bare name → not a method, x.h → a method directly in a class body). ctx is unchanged. Fields not on the model (such as meta) are still opaque.
(C) R2-r3-3: a narrowing change that removes units. It narrows to one definition only when the name resolves uniquely under the same conditions as D61 G3. Specifically: exactly one module-level binding, not in _scan_module_writes, and "*" not in writes; the name not bound locally in any enclosing function or lambda, and a class body is not the innermost scope; imports resolved strictly by level; an absolute import only when exactly one in-tree module matches (to avoid getting script-style `from handlers import h` wrong); re-exports followed under the same conditions; `m.h` only when m is a module import. Anything else falls back to the existing bare-name match, with test candidates removed when the registration is not in a test file. Not checked: `setattr(sys.modules[...])`, and overwriting via another module's attribute (`srv.handle = x`).
(D) R2-r3-2 / R2-r4-1: the number of units goes up (add_request_handler's handler= or last positional argument, and Server resolved from an aliased import). on_call_tool= is still required.
